Good morning! I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply a 10-question check-in that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally since your baby arrived. Anything you share stays between us; the goal is to give you a safe, judgment-free space. We’ll go one question at a time, touching on the past seven days. Ready to start?

Over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Yeah… I can still laugh sometimes. When my husband makes a silly face at the baby I’ll chuckle, but it feels kind of muted—like the laughter doesn’t last or feel as bright as it used to before she was born.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes, I guess… I can laugh if something’s really funny, but mostly it feels kind of flat—like I’m going through the motions rather than really feeling it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to little things—like my mom bringing over dinner or taking the baby for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It’s more “that’ll be nice” than “I can’t wait.”
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week. Like when she wouldn’t settle for her nap, I kept thinking maybe I’m not reading her cues right or that a “better mom” would know how to soothe her faster. I know it’s probably not fair, but the thought still pops in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just get this tight feeling in my chest out of nowhere—like something bad might happen to the baby even when she’s perfectly fine. It usually passes if I take a few deep breaths, but it’s unsettling while it lasts.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky… more like a sudden “what if?” rush—like if she coughs or startles, my heart jumps and I imagine worst-case stuff for a second. It’s quick, not a full-blown scare, but it leaves me jittery for a few minutes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… some days it feels as if the dishes, laundry, and feedings just pile up faster than I can handle them. I manage to get through, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water and I end those days exhausted and teary.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really… I can fall asleep most nights, though sometimes I lie there running through the day and worrying I forgot something. Once I’m out I sleep okay, but getting my brain to quiet down can take a while.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I do feel sad some of the day—like a heavy feeling that just sits there even when nothing bad is happening. It’s not constant, but it comes and goes, especially in the evenings when everything finally quiets down.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when she wouldn’t latch and I felt like I was failing her, and another night when I was just exhausted and couldn’t explain why I was upset. The tears don’t last long, but they come out of nowhere and leave me feeling kind of empty.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, not at all. I’ve never thought about hurting myself—I just want to feel like myself again so I can be there for my daughter.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2 wks post-delivery

Areas endorsed (EPDS‐10 pattern):
- Mild anhedonia & reduced capacity for pleasure (Q1, Q2)
- Frequent self-blame / guilt over infant care (Q3)
- Episodic, unprovoked anxiety and “what-if” catastrophic worries about infant safety (Q4, Q5)
- Persistent sadness/mood heaviness, worse evenings; crying spells triggered by feeding fatigue (Q8, Q9)
- Feeling overwhelmed and “barely keeping head above water,” with end-of-day tearfulness (Q6)
- Initial insomnia due to rumination (Q7)

Denies:
- Panic attacks, self-harm ideation, or thoughts of harming infant (Q5, Q10)

Screening significance:
Symptoms cluster consistent with mild-to-moderate postpartum depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety. No current safety concerns.

Next step: Recommend formal EPDS scoring, clinical interview for major depressive episode with peripartum onset, and psychoeducation/support options.
